newsitem.title: MEXICO: Zapatista supporters in Mexico see civil war risk.
newsitem.headline: Zapatista supporters in Mexico see civil war risk.

text.p: The political arm of Mexico's Zapatista rebels said on Wednesday the country was on the verge of civil war after the virtual breakdown of peace talks in the southeastern state of Chiapas.

Leaders of the newly formed Zapatista National Liberation Front (FZLN) read a statement at a news conference accusing the government of President Ernesto Zedillo of leading the 18-month-old peace talks "down a dead-end street."
"Now the country is once again on the verge of a civil war," the statement said.

The FZLN is the newly formed political wing of the Zapatista National Liberation Army, which rose up in a struggle for indigenous rights and democracy in Chiapas in January 1994. There was only a brief burst of fighting, and since then peace talks have lurched forward with occasional breaks.

On Monday Zapatista rebel leader Subcommander Marcos announced that his forces were pulling out of the talks until the government was prepared to negotiate seriously. The government said the break was only a temporary suspension.

FZLN leader Javier Elorriaga, recently freed from a Chiapas jail in which he had been held on charges of rebellion, accused the government of failing to deliver what it had promised in a February accord on indigenous rights.
"The accords continue to be just paper," he said.
The Zapatistas have often used bellicose language in confronting the government, but since the early days of their uprising, they have barely fired a shot.

Their position has been complicated, however, by the emergence elsewhere in southern Mexico in the last two months of a new rebel force called the Popular Revolutionary Army (EPR). On Friday it launched a series of attacks in which at least 14 people were killed.
Marcos has distanced himself and his rebel force from the EPR, saying the Zapatistas were fighting for "democracy, freedom and justice," while the rival rebels were after power.
